name: Nifty200 Momentum 30 index rules (ETF or DIY)
rule: Each June and December, among Nifty 200 stocks listed 1+ year and in F&O: MR6 = 6-month return / 1-year annualised daily volatility; MR12 likewise with 12-month return. Z-score both cross-sectionally; Z = 0.5*Z6 + 0.5*Z12; score = 1+Z if Z>=0 else 1/(1-Z). Hold top 30; weight = free-float cap x score, capped at min(5%, 5x free-float weight). Or hold a Nifty200 Momentum 30 ETF.

params.rank_buffer: applied by NSE, values not verified

instruments: Nifty200 Momentum 30 ETF or index fund; or Nifty 200 constituent stocks
reported_performance: NSE price index Apr 2005 to 27 Feb 2026 (back-tested before Aug 2020 launch): 19.19% p.a. vs Nifty 200 15.08%; max drawdown 68% vs 64%; calendar 2025 -4.57% (14.13 points behind Nifty 200); fell 31.8% from 27 Sep 2024 to 7 Apr 2025.
feasibility_reason: One ETF order (about Rs 106 per full round trip at Rs 1.5 lakh, no per-stock DP charges, churn untaxed inside the fund). DIY with 30 stocks at Rs 5,000 each is marginal: about 0.93% per round trip plus whole-share rounding.

name: Capitalmind naive momentum: top 30 by 12-month return, monthly
rule: First trading day of each month: rank all liquid NSE stocks (include delisted names) by 252-day price return. Buy the top N equal weight; sell names that drop out; repeat monthly. Ranking variants: (share of up days in 252 days) x (252-day return), or 252-day excess return divided by annualised daily volatility. Long only, no stops, no cash rule.
holding_period: 1 month re-rank; names typically last 2 to 6 months
reported_performance: Backtest Jan 2007 to 2019, no costs or tax: simple 12.6% p.a., gain-loss 14.7%, volatility-adjusted 16.8% vs Nifty 8.9% and Nifty 500 8.7%; beat the indices in 6 of 13 years; deeper drawdown than the index in 2008. Jan 2000 to May 2020: Rs 100 to Rs 1,038 after tax vs Nifty Rs 602 (as quoted by PrimeInvestor).
feasibility_reason: 30 names at Rs 5,000 cost about 0.93% per round trip and are re-ranked monthly. Workable only with 10 to 15 names and a rank buffer; every gain is taxed at 20% STCG.

name: Capitalmind-style volatility-adjusted momentum with minimum hold and cash rule
rule: Weekly: score the top-500 liquid NSE stocks by volatility-adjusted composite momentum (stand-in: 12- and 6-month return over volatility). Candidates are the top decile. Hold 15-25 names weighted by rank and inverse volatility. Replace a holding only after a 1-month minimum hold, when it fails retention or a stronger candidate appears. Hold cash when too few candidates qualify or the broad market is declining.

params.score: proprietary; stand-in sharpe of 12m and 6m returns

instruments: NSE cash equities; liquid ETF when in cash
reported_performance: PMS live since 5 Mar 2019, net of fees, to 6 Nov 2026: 7y 17.8% p.a. vs Nifty 50 TRI 12.4%; 5y 7.0% vs 8.3%; 3y 7.9% vs 10.1%; 2y -5.9% vs 2.3%; 1y 6.6% vs -0.8%. Smallcase 3y CAGR 14.91% at closure (factsheet 6 Oct 2025).
feasibility_reason: Retail product closed (smallcase ended 30 Sep 2025; PMS minimum Rs 50 lakh). A DIY clone at 15-20 names turns over about 20% a month: about 2% a year in charges at Rs 7,500 positions, plus 20% STCG.

name: Weekend Investing Mi India Top 10 style: Nifty 50 top-10 momentum, monthly
rule: Monthly on the last trading day's close: rank Nifty 50 stocks by momentum (formula undisclosed; stand-in 12-month return skipping the last month). Hold 10 at 10% each. Let winners run; sell a holding only if it meets the exit criterion (stand-in: rank worse than 20) and replace it with the best-ranked non-holding. Trade on the first trading day of the next month.
reported_performance: Manager-reported: Covid fall (Feb-Mar 2020) -26% vs Nifty -38.4%; live CAGR is login-gated. Fee Rs 6,999 a year; smallcase minimum Rs 86,228 (Nov 2026).
feasibility_reason: 10 positions of Rs 15,000 in India's most liquid stocks; about 0.62% per swap; low churn. Only if self-built: the subscription alone is 4.7% of capital.

name: Weekend Investing Mi NNF10 style: Nifty Next 50 top-10 momentum, monthly, always invested
rule: Monthly on the last trading day's close: rank Nifty Next 50 stocks by momentum (formula undisclosed; stand-in 6- or 12-month return). Always hold the top 10, never cash; drop losers and add new leaders on the first trading day of the next month. The published version resets each holding to 10% monthly; at small size trade only entries and exits.
reported_performance: Manager-reported, Apr 2016 to Nov 2022 (backtest, live from 12 Nov 2020): CAGR 21.1% vs Nifty Next 50 13.3%; max drawdown 23.6% vs 42%.
feasibility_reason: 10 positions; smallcase minimum Rs 1,14,341 fits; about 0.62% per swap. Self-build only (fee is about 6.7% of capital). Weights will be uneven because of high-priced shares.

name: Weekend Investing Mi 20 / Mi 35 style: weekly rotational momentum in mid and small caps
rule: Weekly: rank stocks in the Nifty MidSmallcap 400 (Mi 20) or Nifty Smallcap 250 (Mi 35) by momentum (formula undisclosed). Hold the strongest N equal weight (20 at 5% each, or up to 35). Stay invested regardless of market conditions. At each weekly review remove holdings that meet the exit criterion and replace them with the next strongest.
instruments: NSE mid and small cap stocks
holding_period: weekly check; weeks to months per stock
reported_performance: Manager-reported: Mi 20, 1 Apr 2016 to 25 Nov 2022, CAGR 26.8% vs MidSmallcap 400 16%, return/max-drawdown 0.7 vs 0.3. Mi 35 CAGR from Apr 2016 to 31 Mar 2020 9.7% vs Smallcap 250 -9%.
feasibility_reason: 20 to 35 positions of Rs 4,300 to 7,500 rotated weekly: 0.8% to 1.2% per swap, smallcase minimums Rs 2.04 to 2.64 lakh, small-cap slippage. Survivorship bias inflates small-cap backtests by about 5 points a year.

name: Weekend Investing Mi 25 / Mi MT Allcap style: absolute momentum, cash when nothing qualifies
rule: Weekly: among liquid stocks above Rs 1,000 crore market cap, a stock qualifies on absolute momentum (stand-in: close above 200-day average, 6-month return positive, near 52-week high). Hold up to N qualifiers equal weight (25 at 4%, or 20 at 5%). Exit when the exit criterion triggers (stand-in: close below 100-day average). Unfilled slots sit in a liquid ETF.
holding_period: weekly check; weeks to months per stock
reported_performance: Manager-reported, Mi 25, Apr 2016 to Jan 2023: +506% vs Smallcap 250 +134%, CAGR 30.2%; Jan 2018 to Mar 2020 fall 29% vs 55%.
feasibility_reason: The cash rule suits a small account, but 20 to 25 weekly-reviewed small caps is too many (minimums Rs 1.96 to 1.99 lakh). Test with 8 to 12 names.

name: Weekend Investing Mi ATH style: stocks at all-time highs, weekly, cash otherwise
rule: Weekly: among NSE stocks above Rs 500 crore market cap with very high turnover, select by momentum rank and nearness to the all-time or multi-year high (stand-in: close within 5% of highest close). Hold up to 10, equal weight. Drop names that fail the exit criterion (stand-in: 15% off peak or below 50-day average). If no new picks qualify, hold a liquid ETF.
reported_performance: Manager-reported: CAGR since 2016 above 40%; Covid fall (Feb-Mar 2020) -16% vs Nifty 500 -38.3%; described as very high churn.
feasibility_reason: 10 positions fit (minimum Rs 1,04,339) and it holds cash in weak markets, but very high churn at about 0.62% per round trip and 20% STCG on every gain.

name: Weekend Investing Mi EverGreen style: 75% momentum stocks, 25% gold ETF
rule: Hold 25% in a gold ETF permanently. With the other 75% hold the 20 strongest-momentum Nifty 200 stocks at about 3.75% each (ranking undisclosed). At each monthly rebalance remove holdings that meet the exit criterion and add the strongest non-holdings. For small accounts scale the stock sleeve to 8-10 names.
reported_performance: Manager-reported: Covid fall (Feb-Mar 2020) -18.7% vs Nifty 200 -38.2%; worst backtest fall -41.27% vs Nifty -59%.
feasibility_reason: As specified it needs about Rs 3.1 lakh (20 stocks plus gold). A scaled version with 8 stocks plus a gold ETF fits.

name: Static Nifty and gold allocation with periodic rebalance (NG5050)
rule: Hold 50% Nifty 50 ETF and 50% gold ETF; rebalance back to equal weight monthly. Variant: 25% each in large-cap, mid-cap and small-cap ETFs and gold. For small accounts rebalance quarterly or only when weights drift by 5 points.
reported_performance: About 15.2% CAGR over roughly 3 years to Oct 2024 for NG5050 (second-hand forum quote). Buy and hold over about 11 years to Nov 2025: Nifty +214% (38% drawdown), GoldM +161% (21% drawdown).
feasibility_reason: Two ETFs and a few orders a year at about Rs 60 to 110 each; no subscription. It is the benchmark the other strategies must beat after costs and tax.

name: Stock momentum with a broad-market trend overlay (MWM Momentum style)
rule: Weekly: rank liquid NSE stocks by price momentum; hold the top 20 equal weight; cut names that fall out of the ranks. Apply a trend filter on the broad market (stand-in: Nifty 500 close above its 200-day average). When the filter is off, move the portfolio to a liquid ETF and stop new buys.
reported_performance: MWM Momentum smallcase, live data only: 14.7% 3-year CAGR at 4 Aug 2025 (launched 14 Apr 2020); not independently validated.
feasibility_reason: Same cost problem as any 20-name weekly momentum book; the Rs 12,001 fee is 8% of capital, so self-build with 10 to 12 names.

name: Low-liquidity half of the top-30 momentum names, annual rebalance
rule: Once a year: rank Nifty 200 stocks by 12-month return and take the top 30. Compute scaled turnover = average daily traded value / market capitalisation. Buy the 15 with the lowest scaled turnover, equal weight. Hold 12 months, then repeat.
reported_performance: Dec 2006 to Jun 2025, net of brokerage, slippage and tax: low-turnover half 19.43% CAGR (max drawdown -66.41%); all 30 names 14.60% (-70.61%); high-turnover half 8.51% (-75.09%); Nifty 50 10.41% (-55.12%).
feasibility_reason: 15 positions of Rs 10,000 with one round trip a year (about 0.69%) and mostly long-term gains. Expect drawdowns above 60%; single-author result.

name: Dual momentum between a Nifty ETF, a gold ETF and debt
rule: At each check (month end; variant quarter end) compute trailing return (12 months; variants 3 months or 200 days) for a Nifty ETF, a gold ETF and a debt or liquid benchmark. If Nifty beats debt, hold whichever of Nifty and gold has the higher return; otherwise hold the debt or liquid fund. One asset at a time; switch at the next open.
instruments: NIFTYBEES, GOLDBEES, liquid ETF or fund
reported_performance: Monthly 12-month version Dec 1996 to Jan 2024: 14.0% vs Nifty 12.4%, drawdown about 21% vs 50%+ (no costs). 200-day version 2014-2024: 18.79% vs 12.13%. Quarterly 3-month version re-run with 0.5% switch cost, Mar 2007 to Dec 2024: 9.11% CAGR, -29.7% drawdown, worse than holding either asset.
feasibility_reason: One ETF order each way (about Rs 106 per full switch). The main drag is 20% STCG on every profitable switch made within a year.

name: Daily Supertrend(10,3) long-only on Nifty via ETF
rule: On Nifty daily bars compute Supertrend (ATR 10, multiplier 3). Buy the Nifty ETF at the next open when the close is above the Supertrend line; sell at the next open when the close is below it. Long only; cash or liquid ETF when out. Comparison variant: 8-day EMA price cross.
instruments: Nifty 50 ETF (index futures need more capital)
holding_period: weeks to months; about 4 trades a year
reported_performance: Nifty spot Jan 2015 to Oct 2025, no costs: 44 long trades averaging 270 points (8-EMA variant 256 trades averaging 35 points); short side lost; Supertrend drawdown about 70% deeper than the EMA variant.
feasibility_reason: About 4 ETF round trips a year at about Rs 106 each. The futures version does not fit (margin about Rs 2.2 lakh, notional about Rs 19 lakh).

name: Hourly Supertrend(10,3) long-only on Nifty and gold, 50:50
rule: On 1-hour bars compute Supertrend(10,3) separately for Nifty and gold. For each, go long at the next bar's open after a close above the line; exit at the next bar's open after a close below it. Long only. Allocate half the capital to each sleeve.
instruments: Nifty and MCX GoldM futures; NIFTYBEES and GOLDBEES as substitutes
reported_performance: About 11 years to Nov 2025, unlevered, no costs: Nifty sleeve +205%, GoldM +169%, 50:50 +187% with 6.6% max drawdown (18.5% and 11.8% for the sleeves); buy and hold Nifty +214% with a 38% drawdown.
feasibility_reason: Futures need about Rs 3.45 lakh margin (Rs 15.75 lakh at 2x leverage). The ETF substitute fits but needs hourly data, far more trades and pays 20% STCG.

name: Donchian 20-day breakout and 5x20 SMA crossover on Nifty
rule: Donchian: go long when the daily close exceeds the prior 20-day high; exit or reverse when it closes below the prior 20-day low. SMA variant: long when the 5-day SMA is above the 20-day SMA; exit or short when below. Test long-short, long only and short only on Nifty daily bars.
reported_performance: Nifty daily, about 10 years to Oct 2025, before costs: long-short Sharpe very poor with negative median trade; long-only Donchian spent 5 years in drawdown; 5x20 long-only made about 7,500 points in 10 years.
feasibility_reason: Fits mechanically with a Nifty ETF, long only. The evidence is negative.

name: Nifty 50 inclusion trade: buy on effective date, hold two weeks
rule: For each stock added to the Nifty 50 at the March or September review (exclude merger and demerger cases): buy at the close on the effective date (first working day after that month's F&O expiry), hold 10 trading days, then sell. Split capital equally if several stocks are added.
instruments: the stock being added to the Nifty 50
reported_performance: 33 inclusions 2015 to 2025, price returns, no costs: 2-week win rate 78.8%, mean +2.21%, median +3.07%; compounded +22.25% over 10 years with 14.3% max drawdown; 6-month median -2.28%.
feasibility_reason: One or two stock trades twice a year at about 0.3% round trip. Adds only about 2% a year, so it is an add-on, not a core strategy.

name: ETF ki Dukan (Mahesh Kaushik): buy the weakest equity ETF daily, sell at +4.57%
rule: Daily after the close, across about 75 liquid equity ETFs (volume above 100,000 units, one per index, no gold or debt): compute RSI(14). Buy one fixed lot of the lowest-RSI ETF not already held; if the five lowest are all held, add to a held ETF only if its price is 3% below its last buy. Sell one lot per day: the most profitable holding at or above +4.57% on average cost.

params.alt_rank: pct below 20-day average | nearness to 52-week low

reported_performance: No independent backtest; evidence is the creator's experience and a 3-month diary. The 2025 variant took a 20% loss on a realty ETF bought repeatedly without price spacing.
feasibility_reason: Rs 20,000 lots cost about 0.38% per round trip against a 4.57% target, but only 7 lots fit in Rs 1.5 lakh and there is no stop, so capital locks up in falling sector ETFs.

name: Mahesh Kaushik's Nifty 50 ETF daily grid (1.57% steps)
rule: Daily at the close, at most one trade. Sell first: among held Nifty 50 ETF lots more than 1.57% above purchase price, sell the one with the largest gain; no buy that day. Otherwise, if the most recently bought lot is more than 1.57% below its purchase price, or has already been sold, buy Rs 20,000 of the highest-ranked Nifty 50 ETF not held. Never average an ETF already held.
reported_performance: Author's backtest 21 Oct 2021 to 19 Oct 2026, no costs or tax: 148 sells, booked Rs 65,697, open loss Rs 13,029 on 12 lots, peak deployed Rs 2,41,536; about 3.5% a year on the Rs 3 lakh fund.
feasibility_reason: Designed for Rs 3 lakh at Rs 20,000 lots; halving the lot doubles the cost share (about Rs 50 on a Rs 220 average gain). Net return is below a liquid fund in the author's own test.

name: Buy the Nifty 50 stock furthest below its 20-day average, sell at +5%
rule: Daily: for each Nifty 50 stock compute (close - 20-day SMA) / 20-day SMA. Buy one fixed lot of the stock furthest below its 20-day average. Sell any holding whose gain exceeds 5%. No stop loss.
reported_performance: Self-reported XIRR 44.91% from Sep 2023 to Apr 2024 (7 bull-market months, unaudited); the author expects 12-24%.
feasibility_reason: Lots of Rs 7,500 to 15,000 cost 0.6% to 0.8% per round trip against a 5% target, but there is no exit for losers, so capital can lock up.

name: V20 pullback: buy the base of a 20% green-candle run, sell at its top
rule: Scan daily bars for a run of 2 or more consecutive green candles that gains at least 20% from the run's lowest low to its highest high. Place a standing limit buy at the run's lowest low for a fixed cash amount. When filled, place a limit sell at the run's highest high. No stop. Optional filter: run base below the 200-day SMA unless the stock is a large cap.
reported_performance: No published statistics found (open-source TradingView script, July 2026).
feasibility_reason: 15 slots of Rs 10,000 at about 0.69% per round trip against a 20% target; no margin or shorting needed. Untested, and capital can sit in unfilled or stuck orders.

name: 9:20 intraday short straddle with per-leg stops
rule: At 09:20 sell the at-the-money call and put of the current weekly Nifty expiry, one lot each. Place a stop on each leg at entry premium x 1.25 (variants 1.35, 1.40). If one leg stops out, keep the other with its stop. Square off everything at 15:10-15:15.
reported_performance: About 1,300 trades over 5 years to May 2022 were profitable with 25% stops but negative once the top 10% of trades are removed; the Bank Nifty version's edge diminished in 2023; a no-stop Nifty test in Dec 2024 was positive on 12 of 20 days (about +434 points before costs).
feasibility_reason: Margin about Rs 2.36 lakh per lot (Feb 2025). Four orders a day cost about Rs 135, roughly 22% of Rs 1.5 lakh a year. Stops get hunted; 91% and 87.7% of retail F&O traders lost in FY25 and FY26.

name: Hedged option selling: 9:20 iron fly and iron condor
rule: Iron fly: at 09:20 sell the at-the-money Nifty weekly call and put and buy the call 300 points above and the put 300 points below. Iron condor: sell a call and a put about 300 points out of the money and buy wings further out. Stop each short leg at a fixed percentage of premium or exit at a combined-premium target; square off by 15:10 or hold to expiry.
reported_performance: No published track record found. Margin example, Feb 2025: Rs 93,741 for a one-lot iron fly vs Rs 2,36,316 unhedged.
feasibility_reason: One lot fits on margin, but eight orders a day cost about Rs 235 (about 38% of capital a year if run daily); a weekly hold-to-expiry version costs far less but has no evidence.

name: 15-minute opening range breakout
rule: Record the high and low of the first 15 minutes (09:15-09:30). Buy when price breaks above the range high (optionally short below the range low). Stop at the opposite side of the range; exit at a fixed target or at the close. One trade per day.
instruments: index futures or options; liquid stocks intraday
reported_performance: Listed among the six most automated retail strategies (AlgoTest, Mar 2026); no performance published.
feasibility_reason: The intraday equity version fits (about 0.08% to 0.13% per round trip at Rs 1,00,000 to 50,000); index derivative versions hit lot and margin limits. Needs intraday data and execution.

name: 9 EMA / 20 EMA crossover
rule: Buy when the 9-period EMA crosses above the 20-period EMA; sell (or reverse) when it crosses below. Timeframe is a parameter (5-minute, 15-minute or daily).
instruments: any liquid stock, ETF or index derivative
reported_performance: No performance published by the platform. Closest Indian tests: an 8-EMA price cross on Nifty daily made 35 points a trade over 256 long trades (Jan 2015 to Oct 2025, before costs); a 5x20 SMA cross was judged not tradable.
feasibility_reason: Runs on a single ETF with small orders; cost depends on timeframe. Related Indian evidence is weak to negative.

name: Intraday mean reversion to VWAP or Bollinger middle band
rule: Intraday on liquid stocks: short when price is stretched above session VWAP by a threshold, or touches the upper Bollinger band (20 periods, 2 standard deviations); cover at VWAP or the middle band. Mirror rule for longs. Flat by the close. Thresholds and stops are user parameters.
instruments: liquid NSE stocks intraday; index derivatives
reported_performance: No performance published. One long-time forum systematic trader says intraday mean reversion and momentum in stocks are both feasible and scalping probably is not (no numbers).
feasibility_reason: Intraday equity permits shorting and leverage at about 0.05% to 0.13% per round trip, but per-trade edges are small and it needs intraday data and fast execution.

name: SIP timing on a Nifty ETF: buy dips, or only above/below the 200-day average
rule: Each month park the instalment in a liquid fund. Deploy into a Nifty ETF only when a dip signal fires: index below its 200-day (or 10-month) average, or a daily fall or gap-down of at least X% (X from 0 to 4). Variant: deploy at month end if no signal fired. Never sell. Compare with a plain monthly SIP.
reported_performance: Nifty 50, about 1994 to 2024: 0 of 152 dip rules beat the monthly SIP (12.04% XIRR); the most selective rules earned 8.65%. Sensex TRI, 122 rolling 15-year windows: no difference before tax, worse after.
feasibility_reason: Trivial to run with one ETF, but it concerns deploying new savings rather than growing a fixed pot, and the evidence is negative.

name: DIY capital-protected structure: debt fund plus a long-dated Nifty call
rule: On the first trading day of each year set capital = Nifty spot x lot size. Buy one at-the-money December Nifty call (strike rounded to the nearest 1,000). Invest the remainder in a liquid or gilt fund. Hold both to the December expiry; repeat.
instruments: Nifty long-dated call option; debt mutual fund
reported_performance: 2019 to 2025 backtest: maximum potential drawdown 6.4% (2022); 2019 liquid+call 9.99% and gilt+call 14.40% vs NIFTYBEES 12.9%; lagged the index in 2025.
feasibility_reason: Needs capital equal to one lot's notional, about Rs 18 lakh.
